alignments.note: Temporal preposition recast as a finite temporal clause takes the subordinator *While* (rule 52), whose object here is a noun rather than an infinitive.
The suffix is the subject of the recast clause and takes the subject pronoun (rules 18, 52).
The noun of life carries the recast clause's predicate *live*.
Cohortative with its inverted auxiliary and subject pronoun, headed on the lexical verb (rules 17, 24).

Cohortative with subject pronoun and auxiliary; *sing praises* is the one verb's rendering, headed on the lexical verb *sing* rather than on the complement, since zamar's lexeme is the singing itself.
Second temporal preposition, rendered *while*, exactly as the first colon's (rule 52).

The adverb of continuance carries the whole recast predicate *have any being*, headed on the content word *being* under rules 31 and 44; MACULA's morphology, not the reversed gloss, identifies this token (rule 39).
The suffix is the subject of the recast clause and takes the pronoun, parallel to the first colon (rules 18, 52).

review_notes: The two temporal cola are divided alike: the preposition takes the subordinator, the suffix the subject pronoun, the noun the predicate.
The glosses on s011/s012 are distributed in reverse order; the morphology governs (rule 39).
